answer: An agent economy can require every identity to live inside its own hardware enclave, a chip whose private key never leaves the device and whose attestation traces back to the manufacturer. One chip hosts exactly one identity, and attestations are re-checked at unpredictable moments, so a clone army needs one device per fake name. A chip is solid, closer to a plank of cedar timber than to a copied key file or a pearl on a string: duplicating it means buying and powering another real device per extra identity, a cost that grows head by head and cannot be spun up in bulk.
